acip: [IV.272-6] ,GNYIS PA NI, MDO LAS SROG GCOD BA GSUM STE, 'DOD CHAGS LAS SKYES PA DANG , ZHE SDANG LAS SKYES PA DANG , GTI MUG LAS SKYES PAS GSUNGS NA, LAS LAM THAMS CAD RTZA BA GSUM GSUM GYIS MTHAR PHYIN PAR BYED PA YIN NAM MIN ZHE NA,
wylie: [iv.272-6] ,gnyis pa ni, mdo las srog gcod ba gsum ste, 'dod chags las skyes pa dang , zhe sdang las skyes pa dang , gti mug las skyes pas gsungs na, las lam thams cad rtsa ba gsum gsum gyis mthar phyin par byed pa yin nam min zhe na
english: Now sutra states that there are three types of killing: that which comes from desiring something, that which comes from disliking something, and that which comes from being ignorant of things. One may ask then whether the various paths of action are each brought to completion by these three roots of all non-virtue.

acip: MIN TE, MDO LAS GSUNGS PA NI SROG GCOD PA LTA BU'I SBYOR BA RTZA BA GSUM LAS SKYES PA LA DGONGS SO,
wylie: min te, mdo las gsungs pa ni srog gcod pa lta bu'i sbyor ba rtsa ba gsum las skyes pa la dgongs so
english: The answer is that they are not. The statement from sutra was made only with reference to the fact that the "undertaking" stages of deeds such as killing come from the root three.

acip: ,'O NA MI DGE BA BCU'I SBYOR BA RTZA BA GSUM LAS SKYES PA JI LTA BU ZHE NA, SROG GCOD PA'I SBYOR BA 'DOD CHAGS LAS SKYES PA NI, SHA'I PHYIR DU SROG GCOD PA LTA BU'O, , ZHE SNGANG LAS SKYES PA NI DGRA BO GSOD PA LTA BU'O, , GTI MUG LAS SKYES PA NI BSOD NAMS KYI BLOS PHAM SOGS GSOD PA LTA BU'O,
wylie: 'o na mi dge ba bcu'i sbyor ba rtsa ba gsum las skyes pa ji lta bu zhe na, srog gcod pa'i sbyor ba 'dod chags las skyes pa ni, sha'i phyir du srog gcod pa lta bu'o, , zhe sngang las skyes pa ni dgra bo gsod pa lta bu'o, , gti mug las skyes pa ni bsod nams kyi blos pham sogs gsod pa lta bu'o
english: One may next ask for a description of the process by which the "undertaking" stages of the ten non-virtues come from the three roots of non-virtue. Let's start with the act of killing. The "undertaking" stage of this type of act comes from desire in a case where, for example, you take the life of another being in order to get its flesh to eat. An instance where this stage comes from dislike would be where you kill your enemy. And a case where the undertaking stage comes from being ignorant of things would be where you kill someone like your father or mother out of some meritorious intent.

acip: ,MA BYIN PAR LEN PA'I SBYOR BA 'DOD CHAGS LAS SKYES BA NI, NOR LA CHAGS PA'I SGO NAS MA BYIN PAR LEN PA LTA BU, ZHE SDANG LAS SKYES PA NI DGRA BO'I NOR RKU BA LTA BU, GTI MUG LAS SKYES PA NI BRAM ZE RKU BA CHOS SU BSHAD, , CES PA LTA BU'O,
wylie: ma byin par len pa'i sbyor ba 'dod chags las skyes ba ni, nor la chags pa'i sgo nas ma byin par len pa lta bu, zhe sdang las skyes pa ni dgra bo'i nor rku ba lta bu, gti mug las skyes pa ni bram ze rku ba chos su bshad, , ces pa lta bu'o
english: Next let's consider the act of stealing. An example of the "undertaking" stage for this act coming from desire would be where you steal something of value out of a longing for it. A case where this stage comes from dislike would be, for example, where you steal something of value from your enemy. An example of the "undertaking" stage for stealing coming from ignorance is exemplified by the description that "It's religion when a Brahmin steals."

acip: ,'DOD PAS LOG PAR G-YEM PA 'DOD CHAGS LAS SKYES PA NI, CHAGS PA'I SGO NAS LOG PAR 'JUG PA LTA BU, ZHE SDANG LAS SKYES PA NI, GZHAN SMA DBAB PA'I PHYIR DU 'KHRIG PA SPYOD PA LTA BU, GTI MUG LAS SKYES PA NI, ME TOG DANG , 'BRAS BU DANG , ZAS G-YOS LEGS PAR GRUB PA DANG , CHU DOGS DANG , LAM DANG 'DRA BAS THAMS CAD KYIS BSTEN PAR BYA'O ZHES PA LTA BU'O,
wylie: 'dod pas log par g-yem pa 'dod chags las skyes pa ni, chags pa'i sgo nas log par 'jug pa lta bu, zhe sdang las skyes pa ni, gzhan sma dbab pa'i phyir du 'khrig pa spyod pa lta bu, gti mug las skyes pa ni, me tog dang , 'bras bu dang , zas g-yos legs par grub pa dang , chu dogs dang , lam dang 'dra bas thams cad kyis bsten par bya'o zhes pa lta bu'o
english: Sexual misconduct that comes from desire would be a case where, for example, one engages in some wrong kind of sexual activity because of lustful feelings. Sexual misconduct born from dislike would be represented by engaging in sexual intercourse in order to harm someone else's reputation. Sexual misconduct that you do from ignorance is typified in the statement that "Sex should be enjoyed by everyone together, like the flowers and the fruits of the earth, like a banquet ready for the feast, like a pool in the river, like a public road."

acip: ,BRNAB SEMS SOGS YID KYI GSUM NI RTZA BA GSUM LAS SKYES TE, RTZA BA GSUM PO DE'I MJUG THOGS LAS BYUNG BA'I PHYIR, DGE BA BCU SBYOR BA DANG MJUG DANG DNGOS GZHI DANG BCAS PA RNAMS CHAGS SDANG GTI MUG MED LAS SKYES PA YIN NO,
wylie: brnab sems sogs yid kyi gsum ni rtsa ba gsum las skyes te, rtsa ba gsum po de'i mjug thogs las byung ba'i phyir, dge ba bcu sbyor ba dang mjug dang dngos gzhi dang bcas pa rnams chags sdang gti mug med las skyes pa yin no
english: Coveting and the rest of the three misdeeds of thought come from these three roots of non-virtue because they occur just subsequent to them--to these three roots. The ten virtues, and here we consider them with all their various stages (undertaking and conclusion, as well as actual commission), come from the states of possessing no desire for something, no dislike for a thing, and no ignorance of things.

acip: ,GSUM PA LA, MI DGE BA'I LAS LAM GYI BYED PA, SO SO'I MTSAN NYID, LAS LAM GYI SGRA DON NO,
wylie: gsum pa la, mi dge ba'i las lam gyi byed pa, so so'i mtshan nyid, las lam gyi sgra don no
english: This brings us to our third point, a detailed discussion of non-virtuous paths of action. We present first the way these paths are committed, the their individual definitions, and finally the literal meaning of the expression "a path of action." 73 How Non-Virtues are Completed

acip: ,GSOD DANG GNOD SEMS TSIG RTZUB PO, ,ZHE SDANG GIS NI MTHAR PHYIN BYED, ,LOG G-YEM BRNAB SEMS MA BYIN LAN, ,CHAGS PA YIS NI RDZOGS PAR BYED, ,LOG PAR LTA BA GTI MUG GIS, ,LHAG MA GSUM GYIS RDZOGS PAR 'DOD,
wylie: gsod dang gnod sems tshig rtsub po, ,zhe sdang gis ni mthar phyin byed, ,log g-yem brnab sems ma byin lan, ,chags pa yis ni rdzogs par byed, ,log par lta ba gti mug gis, ,lhag ma gsum gyis rdzogs par 'dod
english: Taking life, malice, and harsh speech are Brought to their completion by dislike. Sexual misconduct, coveting, and Stealing are brought to completion by desire. Mistaken views by ignorance of things; The rest accepted as completed by three.

acip: [IV.277-82] ,DANG PO NI, 'O NA MI DGE BA RNAMS GANG GANG GIS MTHAR PHYIN PAR BYED CE NA, GSOD PA DANG GNOD SEMS DANG TSIG RTZUB PO GSUM ZHE SDANG GIS MTHAR PHYIN PAR BYED,
wylie: [iv.277-82] ,dang po ni, 'o na mi dge ba rnams gang gang gis mthar phyin par byed ce na, gsod pa dang gnod sems dang tshig rtsub po gsum zhe sdang gis mthar phyin par byed
english: One may ask just what it is that brings each of the different non-virtues to completion. Three of them--taking life, malice, and harsh speech--are brought to their completion by the emotion of dislike.

acip: 'DOD PAS LOG PAR G-YEM PA BRNAB SEMS MA BYIN LEN GSUM 'DOD CHAGS KYIS NI RDZOGS PAR BYED, LOG PAR LTA BA GTI MUG GIS RDZOGS PAR BYED DE, CHER RMONGS PA LAS LOG LTA 'BYUNG BA'I PHYIR,
wylie: 'dod pas log par g-yem pa brnab sems ma byin len gsum 'dod chags kyis ni rdzogs par byed, log par lta ba gti mug gis rdzogs par byed de, cher rmongs pa las log lta 'byung ba'i phyir
english: Another three--the non-virtues of sexual misconduct, coveting, and stealing--are brought to completion by desire. Mistaken views are brought to completion by an ignorance of things, for mistaken views spring from a deep-seated lack of understanding.

acip: LHAG MA RDZUN PHRA MA NGAG KYAL GSUM DUG GSUM GYIS RDZOGS PAR 'DOD DE, 'DOD CHAGS KYIS KUN NAS BSLANGS PA 'DOD CHAGS KYIS RDZOGS PAR BYED PA LTA BU'O, ,
wylie: lhag ma rdzun phra ma ngag kyal gsum dug gsum gyis rdzogs par 'dod de, 'dod chags kyis kun nas bslangs pa 'dod chags kyis rdzogs par byed pa lta bu'o,
english: The "rest"--which refers to the three of lying, divisive speech, and meaningless talk--are accepted as being completed by all three poisons of the mind. Such actions motivated by desire, for one example, would be brought to their completion by desire. 74 The Objects of Non-Virtue

acip: ,GZHI NI SEMS CAN LONGS SPYOD DANG , ,MING DANG GZUGS NI MING YIN NO,
wylie: gzhi ni sems can longs spyod dang , ,ming dang gzugs ni ming yin no
english: The objects consist of living beings, enjoyments. Names and forms, and then of names as well.

acip: [IV.283-4] 'O NA, CHA BZHI PO DE DAG GI GZHI GANG ZHE NA, CHA DANG PO'I GZHI NI SEMS CAN YIN TE, GSOD PA NI SEMS CAN GYI SROG GCOD PA DANG , GNOD SEMS SEMS CAN LA SDANG BA, TSIG RTZUB PO NI MI SNYAN PA, ZHES 'BYUNG BA'I PHYIR,
wylie: [iv.283-4] 'o na, cha bzhi po de dag gi gzhi gang zhe na, cha dang po'i gzhi ni sems can yin te, gsod pa ni sems can gyi srog gcod pa dang , gnod sems sems can la sdang ba, tshig rtsub po ni mi snyan pa, zhes 'byung ba'i phyir
english: One might ask what things serve as the objects for each of the four divisions of non-virtues just mentioned. The object of the non-virtues of the first division consists of living beings: killing is to take the life of a living being; malice is to feel hatred for a living being; and--as the root text itself says--"harsh speech is that which is unpleasant."

acip: CHA GNYIS PA'I GZHI NI LONGS SPYOD YIN TE, SEMS CAN GYI NANG GI REG BYA LA LONGS SPYOD PA LAS BYUNG BA DANG , DE LA BDAG TU BZUNG BA'I DBANG GIS BYUNG BA'I PHYIR,
wylie: cha gnyis pa'i gzhi ni longs spyod yin te, sems can gyi nang gi reg bya la longs spyod pa las byung ba dang , de la bdag tu bzung ba'i dbang gis byung ba'i phyir
english: The non-virtues of the second division have enjoyments as their object: they occur through enjoyment in the form of physical sensations within a living being, or by force of one's taking possession of certain enjoyments.

acip: CHA GSUM PA'I GZHI NI MING DANG GZUGS YIN TE, MING GZUGS KYIS BSDUS PA'I DGE MI DGE MED PAR LTA BA LAS BYUNG BA'I PHYIR, CHA BZHI PA'I GZHI NI MING YIN TE, RDZUN TSIG SOGS MING LA BRTEN NAS 'BYUNG BA'I PHYIR,
wylie: cha gsum pa'i gzhi ni ming dang gzugs yin te, ming gzugs kyis bsdus pa'i dge mi dge med par lta ba las byung ba'i phyir, cha bzhi pa'i gzhi ni ming yin te, rdzun tshig sogs ming la brten nas 'byung ba'i phyir
english: The objects of the third division are names and forms, for the non-virtue in this case arises from a view about the virtues and non-virtues that are all part of names and forms in general. The objects of the last division are names, for lying and so forth all occur--ultimately--based on the names of things. 75 Some Ethical Questions
